underworld.fact: Karl Hyde's cryptic lyrics famously blend stream-of-consciousness poetry with found material, including snippets from overheard conversations and answering-machine recordings.
The band took its name from the 1985 horror film Underworld, which their earlier group Freur had scored.
Before turning to dance music, Hyde and Smith led a synth-pop band called Freur, best known for the 1983 single "Doot-Doot."
Their 2016 album Barbara Barbara, We Face a Shining Future earned a 2017 Grammy nomination for Best Dance/Electronic Album.
The title of their 1999 album Beaucoup Fish comes from a sampled recording of a Cajun fisherman in Louisiana on the track "Jumbo."
Their signature anthem "Born Slippy .NUXX" was originally released only as a B-side, then exploded into a global hit after featuring in the 1996 film Trainspotting.
For their Drift project they released new music every week for 52 weeks in 2018 and 2019, culminating in the critically acclaimed album Drift Series 1.
Underworld directed the music for the opening ceremony of the 2012 London Olympics, reuniting with director Danny Boyle and winning a Q Award for Innovation in Sound.
Underworld formed in 1987 in Cardiff, Wales, and its core duo of Karl Hyde and Rick Smith have made music together since the late 1970s.
In 2018 they released Teatime Dub Encounters, a collaborative EP with punk icon Iggy Pop, born from sessions originally intended for the T2 Trainspotting soundtrack.

carlos-sadness.fact: Before dedicating himself fully to music, he worked as an advertising creative and illustrator for brands such as Carolina Herrera.
His real name is Carlos Alberto Sánchez Uriol, born in Barcelona on 31 March 1984, and he originally performed under the name Shinoflow.
After building a following posting songs online, the newspaper El País named him 'one of the faces to watch for 2009'.
His song 'Amor Papaya' with Mexican artist Caloncho was the most-streamed Spanish indie track on Spotify during 2017.
His 2018 album 'Diferentes Tipos de Luz' reached No. 2 on the Spanish sales chart.
He signed with Sony Music at the end of 2010 and released his first EP, 'Atraes a los relámpagos', in January 2011, establishing himself in the Spanish indie-pop scene.
On his 2016 Mexico debut he sold out the Lunario venue three nights in a row, something no Spanish artist had achieved on a first visit.
Carlos Sadness won a Latin Grammy in 2018 for the album art of 'Diferentes Tipos de Luz', which he designed himself, since he is both a musician and a trained illustrator.
His 2015 album 'La idea salvaje', produced in Glasgow, is a concept album built around a space voyage as a metaphor for two people drifting apart.
His 2020 album 'Tropical Jesus' features collaborations with Manuel Medrano, Crystal Fighters and Bomba Estéreo, and its artwork was entirely illustrated by him.

the-hill-frequencies.fact: For their second album, Routine Break, they teamed up with musician and producer Tone Catalano of the American duo Little Hurricane.
All six songs on their debut, 4000 Miles from Mississippi, are original compositions written in the Hill Country Blues style.
In 2024 they capped this chapter of their career with a raw triple live recording made at La Coquette Blues Bar.
Hot Nasho originally performed as a One Man Band; the duo formed after Patri began sitting in, first playing the washboard and later moving to drums.
Routine Break marked a deliberate shift away from their traditional Hill Country Blues sound toward reaching new audiences.
During the 2020 lockdown they recorded an EP dedicated to the music of Mississippi bluesman Robert Belfour.
In 2021 Nacho founded the Homegrown Musicmakers Movement to help artists with limited means release their music.
The Marbella-based duo is made up of Patri, known as HF Pat, on drums and Nacho, known as Hot Nasho, on guitar and vocals.
The Hill Frequencies are a real-life couple, Patri and Nacho, who perform as a blues duo bringing North Mississippi Hill Country Blues to Spain.
Their debut album, 4000 Miles from Mississippi (2019), helped introduce Hill Country Blues to a Spanish scene where the style had gained little recognition.

taburete.fact: Their third album, Madame Ayahuasca (2018), was unveiled at Madrid's Las Ventas bullring and earned a Latin Grammy nomination for Best Pop/Rock Album.
Taburete was founded in Madrid in 2014 by singer Willy Barcenas and Anton Carreno, who started out playing restaurants and small venues.
The album Dr. Charas is named in homage to the band's drummer nicknamed Manolin, who worked as a doctor at Madrid's La Paz hospital.
The band coined its own tongue-in-cheek genre label, "electrochotis," blending ranchera, bolero, ska, rocksteady and Spanish pop-rock.
In 2017 they teamed up with veteran Spanish rock band Hombres G for a joint tour called "Devuelveme mi joda" that sold out arenas across Spain.
Ahead of the 2018 FIFA World Cup they released an unofficial anthem for the tournament titled "Desde Rusia con amor."
Their second album, Dr. Charas (2016), went double platinum in Spain, selling around 80,000 copies at a tough time for the record industry.
Frontman Willy Barcenas is the son of Luis Barcenas, the former treasurer of Spain's People's Party, and in the band's early days the press often dubbed them "the son of Barcenas's group."
For their March 2017 concert at Madrid's Palacio de los Deportes they sold 5,000 tickets in just two hours and eventually filled the arena with about 16,000 people.
Singer Willy Barcenas competed on the second season of Spain's Mask Singer in 2021 disguised as "Platano" (Banana), finishing as runner-up.

gente-de-zona.fact: Their music blends reggaeton with traditional Cuban rhythms, a style sometimes called "cubaton."
In 2015 they scored more hits with "La Gozadera" and "Traidora," both in collaboration with Marc Anthony.
In 2016 they released "Mas Macarena," a new version of Los del Rio's global smash "Macarena."
In 2018 they performed at Chile's Vina del Mar International Song Festival, winning both the Silver and Gold Gaviota awards.
"Bailando" reached number one on Billboard's Top Latin Songs chart in the United States in June 2014.
They collaborated with Jennifer Lopez on the 2017 song "Ni tu ni yo."
Their 2016 album "Visualizate" won a Latin Grammy for Best Tropical Fusion Album.
Gente de Zona shot to global fame on Enrique Iglesias's 2014 hit "Bailando," which topped charts worldwide and won three Latin Grammy Awards.
The Cuban group began in 2000 in Alamar, a Havana neighborhood known as the cradle of Cuban hip hop.

inna-echoes-tour.fact: Since 2017 she has been a coach on the talent show Vocea Romaniei Junior.
Her breakthrough single "Hot" (2008) topped the Romanian charts and became a commercial success across Europe.
Her single "Sun Is Up" won the Eurodanceweb Award, making her the first and only Romanian artist to win it.
With around four million album sales from her first three studio albums, INNA is the best-selling Romanian artist, and The Guardian called her "one of Romania's biggest exports."
She has collaborated with major international artists including Daddy Yankee, Yandel, J Balvin and Sean Paul.
She adopted the stage name Inna in 2008 and released her debut studio album, "Hot," in 2009.
Her 2014 single "Cola Song," a collaboration with J Balvin, was certified Platinum in Spain.
She was born Elena Alexandra Apostoleanu in 1986 in Mangalia, Romania, and studied political science before pursuing music.
Her 2019 album "Yo" was written entirely in Spanish, with INNA taking full creative control.

antonio-orozco.fact: He was born on 23 November 1972 in Hospitalet de Llobregat, near Barcelona, to a working-class family from Osuna in Seville.
He released his debut album 'Un reloj y una vela' in 2000 and has since recorded nine studio albums.
His live show 'Único' ran through theatres for nine months, drawing more than 135,000 spectators across 111 sold-out concerts.
In 2022 he underwent surgery for a vocal cord polyp that nearly cost him his voice, spending months in rehabilitation before he could sing again.
His 2013 album 'Dos orillas' went gold within 24 hours of release and platinum within two weeks.
Antonio Orozco has sold more than 1.5 million records and holds a diamond disc, nine platinum discs and numerous gold discs.
Early in his career he served as an opening act for Ricky Martin on the Latin American leg of his tour, playing shows in Mexico, Puerto Rico and Spain.
He bought his first guitar at 15 after hearing young musicians playing in the streets of Seville's Triana neighbourhood, and he still keeps it today.
He won the 2003 Ondas Award for Best Live Artist and has been nominated for a Latin Grammy for his song 'Estoy hecho de pedacitos de ti'.
He became one of the most popular coaches on Spain's 'La Voz', appearing on the show from 2013 across its various editions.

gloria-trevi.fact: Born Gloria de los Angeles Trevino Ruiz in Monterrey in 1968, she has often been called "the Madonna of Mexico."
Her 1989 debut album "Que Hago Aqui?" produced the breakthrough hit "Dr. Psiquiatra," a number one across Latin America.
One of the best-selling Latin music artists in history, Gloria Trevi has sold over 20 million records worldwide and has been dubbed the "Mexican Queen of Pop" by Rolling Stone.
At age 15 she moved to Mexico City to study performing arts at Televisa's arts center, the CEA.
Her life and career have been dramatized in the 2014 biopic "Gloria" and a 2023 television series.
As a child she was drawn to rock artists such as Led Zeppelin, The Doors and Janis Joplin.
Her 1991 single "Pelo Suelto" was a worldwide success, topping charts across Latin America and in Spain.
In 2018 she was inducted into the Latin Songwriters Hall of Fame.
She has scored four number-one albums on the Billboard Top Latin Albums chart.

solea-morente.fact: She was preparing her solo debut album alongside her father when his death in late 2010 cut the project short.
In 2021 she stepped in front of the camera as a co-presenter of the TVE flamenco documentary series 'Caminos del flamenco', alongside Miguel Poveda.
Her first recorded appearance came as a child in 1991, contributing to her father Enrique Morente's album 'Misa flamenca'.
In 2018 she received the Princesa de Girona Foundation Award for Arts and Letters, honouring her genuine fusion of flamenco with pop and rock.
Though she is heir to the Morente flamenco legacy, she does not call herself a 'cantaora', instead blending flamenco with pop rock and alternative rock.
Soleá Morente is the middle daughter of legendary flamenco singer Enrique Morente and dancer Aurora Carbonell; her older sister is the flamenco star Estrella Morente.
She is also an actress, making her stage debut in the play 'Yerma' in 2014 and appearing in Jonás Trueba's film 'La virgen de agosto'.
Born in Madrid in 1985 and raised in Granada, she lives between the city's historic Albaicín quarter and Madrid.
In 2019 she won the Ojo Crítico prize for modern music, awarded by Spain's national broadcaster RNE.
Her 2015 solo debut 'Tendrá que haber un camino' included two posthumous compositions by her father and featured Los Planetas and Lagartija Nick.

omega-30-aniversario.fact: Omega is a landmark 1996 album by flamenco singer Enrique Morente made with the Granada rock band Lagartija Nick — his most daring and controversial work.
Among the many artists on the album was Enrique Morente's daughter, the flamenco singer Estrella Morente.
The album is regarded as a landmark in the revolution of flamenco, opening paths that were unknown until then.
The recording brought together star flamenco guitarists including Tomatito, Vicente Amigo and Juan Manuel Cañizares.
On 2 December 2016 Morente's three children — Estrella, Soleá and José Enrique — marked the album's 20th anniversary with a concert at Madrid's Sala La Riviera.
The album set poems from Federico García Lorca's 'Poeta en Nueva York' to music alongside reworked songs by Canadian singer-songwriter Leonard Cohen.
Omega boldly blended flamenco singing with punk and alternative rock, an unprecedented fusion for its time.
Omega was released in 1996 by the label El Europeo Música and was reissued in 2008.
Leonard Cohen, whose songs feature on Omega, later returned the admiration: the posthumous volume of his poems 'The Flame' includes a piece titled 'Homage to Morente'.
Such was the album's impact that Morente and Lagartija Nick reunited to perform Omega live, including at Barcelona's Primavera Sound in 2008 and on a tour that reached Mexico.

antonito-molina.fact: In 'El Tren de los Sueños' he first performed alongside his partner Álex and later, for nearly six years, with Sevillian singer Mara.
He describes his own style as 'popero muy andaluz' (very Andalusian pop) with a singer-songwriter sensibility.
He decided to go solo in 2016 to sing in a freer, more personal style, saying that staying in the group would have meant 'stagnating'.
He was chosen as the herald (pregonero) of the Cadiz Carnival 2025, a great honour in his home region.
He wrote the songs 'Suéltate el pelo' and 'El hombre de la carpeta' as heartfelt tributes to his mother and father respectively.
He was born and raised in Rota, in the province of Cádiz, and his full name is Antonio Caballero Molina.
His stage name 'Molina' comes from his mother's surname.
Spanish singer Pastora Soler is his artistic godmother and has been one of the biggest supporters of his solo career.
Antoñito Molina began his musical career in the Andalusian pop duo 'El Tren de los Sueños', which he co-founded, before leaving after ten years in 2016 to launch his solo career.

ivan-ferreiro.fact: His solo debut album, "Canciones para el tiempo y la distancia" (2005), reached number 14 on the Spanish albums chart.
He wrote the song "Cancion de amor y muerte" specifically for the horror film "Rec 3."
In 2005 he sang "Lady Blue" with Enrique Bunbury on the show Freak Show, boosting his profile as a solo artist.
His 2011 album "Confesiones de un artista de mierda" was recorded live and featured guests such as Xoel Lopez and Love of Lesbian's Santi Balmes.
He was born in Nigran, in the province of Pontevedra, in 1970, and is a leading figure in Spanish indie music.
In 2018 he released "Cena recalentada," a tribute album to the Galician band Golpes Bajos.
Ivan Ferreiro spent thirteen years as the singer, leader and main songwriter of the influential Galician indie band Los Piratas before launching a solo career.
He was one of the first well-known Spanish artists to offer an album as a free online download, sharing "Mentiroso mentiroso" (2008) via his blog before its release.
After Los Piratas broke up in 2003, he began performing with his brother Amaro at a pub in Vigo.

sidecars.fact: The band won the Premio de la Música for Best Alternative Rock Album in 2009 and a La Noche en Vivo award for Best Breakthrough Group in 2008.
Their self-titled 2008 debut album featured collaborations from both members of the band Pereza, Leiva and Rubén Pozo.
Their song 'Fan de ti', from the 2010 album 'Cremalleras', gained wide exposure after being used in an El Corte Inglés advertising campaign.
In 2022 they wrote 'Si me ves aparecer', the main theme for the Christmas film 'Reyes contra Santa'.
Frontman Juancho is the younger brother of Leiva (of the band Pereza), who produced Sidecars' first two albums.
Their 2016 album 'Contra las cuerdas' was recorded live at Madrid's Sala But with guest stars including Dani Martín, Iván Ferreiro and Carlos Tarque of M Clan.
Sidecars is a Spanish rock band formed in 2006 in the Alameda de Osuna neighbourhood of Madrid.
The band is a trio: Juancho on lead guitar and vocals, Dr. Gerbass on bass, and Ruly on drums.
The band cites influences ranging from The Rolling Stones and Tom Petty to Spanish acts like Tequila, Los Rodríguez and Pereza.
The band emerged from the same Madrid neighbourhood as Pereza, for whom they served as an opening act early in their career.

julio-botti-quartet.fact: His album "Tango Nostalgias," released on Zoho Music, was arranged by Pablo Ziegler and recorded largely in Buenos Aires.
A turning point came in 2008 when he met pianist Pablo Ziegler, Piazzolla's longtime collaborator, who became his mentor.
Argentine saxophonist Julio Botti is regarded as a fresh new voice of the nuevo tango movement pioneered by maestro Astor Piazzolla.
He studied at a conservatory in Havana in 2002 and began performing in Madrid in 2003.
He played in Pablo Ziegler's band during 2009, deepening his passion for expressing tango through the saxophone.
Because the saxophone was never traditionally part of tango, Botti approaches the genre as "a universal jazz language."
He grew up in the town of Bell Ville, in the province of Cordoba, Argentina, joining his first music school after being inspired by local marching bands.
In 1998 he moved to New York to study tenor saxophone with jazz musicians Donny McCaslin and Bob Franceschini.

nile-rodgers-chic.fact: Rodgers is an inductee of both the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and the Songwriters Hall of Fame.
In 2023 he won two more Grammys for his work on Beyonce's "Renaissance" and received the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award.
He co-founded Chic in 1977 with bassist Bernard Edwards; the pair had started out in 1972 as the Big Apple Band.
Chic's "Le Freak" sold more than seven million copies and was Atlantic Records' only triple-platinum single at the time.
Chic's 1979 hit "Good Times" became one of the most-sampled songs of all time, and its groove powered the Sugarhill Gang's "Rapper's Delight," the first multi-platinum hip hop single.
As a producer, Nile Rodgers shaped era-defining albums including David Bowie's "Let's Dance" and Madonna's "Like a Virgin."
Records that Rodgers has written, produced or played on have sold more than 750 million albums and 100 million singles worldwide.
With Bernard Edwards he also wrote and produced "We Are Family" for Sister Sledge and "I'm Coming Out" and "Upside Down" for Diana Ross.
He won three Grammy Awards in 2014 for his work on Daft Punk's "Random Access Memories," including co-writing the global hit "Get Lucky."
He plays a beloved 1960 Fender Stratocaster nicknamed "The Hitmaker," which he picked up as a trade-in at a shop in Miami Beach.

miss-caffeina.fact: They composed "Cuando acabe el verano," the 2024 official theme song of the Vuelta a Espana cycling race, performing it live after the final stage.
The pop band was formed in Madrid in 2006.
The title of their 2019 album "Oh Long Johnson" comes from the viral talking-cat video, chosen as a reminder of how people focus on absurd things while important things pass by.
Their 2019 album "Oh Long Johnson" reached number one on the Spanish albums chart.

In their early days they self-released their EPs directly online, building a following and playing many festivals before recording their first studio album - which didn't arrive until five years after the band formed.
They competed in Benidorm Fest 2024 with the song "Bla bla bla," qualifying for the final of Spain's Eurovision selection.
Their debut studio album, "Imposibilidad Del Fenomeno," was released in 2010.
The band's name comes from a song by the group Buenas Noches Rose; founders Alvaro and Sergio met on that band's online fan forum and started going to all its concerts together.
Mainstream success came in 2016 with their album "Detroit," after the band had already been active for more than a decade.

alvaro-de-luna.fact: As a child he played local concerts covering songs by the Spanish band Jarabe de Palo, which he cites as a major influence.
He was born in Seville on 28 September 1994 and began singing his own songs with a guitar before he was ten years old.
His debut solo album, "Levantaremos al sol," was released in 2022 and gathered together his early solo singles.
With Sinsinati, his songs "Indios y vaqueros" and "Cuando éramos dos" climbed to the top of Canal Fiesta Radio's Top 50.
He plays pop rock and is a self-taught guitarist who has written and composed his own material since childhood.
He recorded the duet "Mañana" with Spanish pop star Lola Indigo.
Before going solo, he was the lead singer and songwriter of the Spanish pop band Sinsinati from 2017 to 2020.
His breakout solo single "Juramento eterno de sal" (2020) became a trend on Spotify and launched his solo career.
He teamed up with two of Spain's biggest stars, Pablo Alborán and Aitana, on the 2021 song "Llueve sobre mojado."
He is often nicknamed "El Cantante de la Voz Rota" (The Singer with the Broken Voice) for his distinctive raspy vocals.

pastora-soler.fact: Her 2017 album 'La calma' debuted at number one on the Spanish album chart, the first number one of her career.
The tour for her 2007 album 'Toda mi verdad' took her to Egypt, where she performed at the Cairo Opera House.
Born María del Pilar Sánchez Luque in Coria del Río, Seville, in 1978, she began singing coplas and flamenco at events as a child.
Her music blends traditional Spanish copla and flamenco with pop and electronic sounds.
Pastora Soler represented Spain at the Eurovision Song Contest 2012 in Baku with 'Quédate conmigo', finishing 10th with 97 points.
She was signed to a record label at just 15 and released her debut album 'Nuestras coplas' in 1994, a collection of classic copla covers.
Her album 'Toda mi verdad' won the Spanish Premio de la Música for Best Copla Album, an honour her live album '15 años' also later received.
Beyond her recording career, she has served as a mentor or coach on Spanish TV talent shows including La Voz Kids and La Voz Senior.
Her first big hit, 'Dámelo ya' (1999), sold 120,000 copies in Spain and also reached number one in Turkey.
In 2014 she put her career on hold citing stage fright, after fainting on stage during a concert in Seville.

galvan-real.fact: His recordings have earned Gold, Platinum, Double Platinum and Triple Platinum certifications.
Galvan Real is the stage name of Oscar Espinosa Castillo, a Spanish singer-songwriter and producer born in Valencia in 1992.
He is known for his unmistakable raspy voice, which has become one of his signature traits.
His best-known songs include "La Magia," "La Luna," "Amigos," "Volverte a Ver" and "Tu Velero."
He has collaborated with artists including Maria Artes, Pyllo Cortes, Calero, Raul Camacho and Borja Rubio.
Since 2012 he has fused flamenco with contemporary urban rhythms such as reggaeton and bachata, creating a distinctive personal style.
Known for high-energy, emotional live shows, he regularly sells out concerts across Spain.

la-plazuela.fact: The name La Plazuela comes from "La Plazuela Techa" (the little roofed plaza) - a spare room in bandmate El Nitro's apartment building where friends gathered to jam, which became their improvised studio and hangout spot.
Their first EP, "Yunque, Clavos y Alcayatas," was released in 2019.
Formed in 2019, the duo's sound is a fusion of flamenco, funk, pop and electronic music.
Their flamenco side draws on the genre's early greats, including Camaron, Enrique Morente, Pata Negra and Ketama.
As teenagers (around age 16), they started out making covers of admired artists such as Manzanita, Los Chichos and Pata Negra.
Their funk influences include modern acts like Silk Sonic, Jungle and Free Nationals.
The Granada duo - Manuel Hidalgo Sierra ("El Indio") and Luis Abril Martin ("El Nitro") - first met as three-year-olds in the same class.
Their debut studio album, "Roneo Funk Club" (2023), was released on Universal Music Spain and co-produced by Juanito Makande.

gipsy-kings.fact: They perform mostly in Spanish but also mix in Catalan, French and Occitan.
In 1990 they were named Group of the Year at France's Victoires de la Musique awards.
They recorded a Spanish-language flamenco version of "You've Got a Friend in Me" for the 2010 film "Toy Story 3."
The band was founded in 1979 in Arles, France, and its members are of Catalan Romani (gitano) heritage.
The group grew out of two families, the Reyes and the Baliardo; fittingly, "reyes" means "kings" in Spanish.
Their flamenco-style cover of the Eagles' "Hotel California" was featured in the 1998 film "The Big Lebowski."
Their parents were gitanos who fled Spain during the 1930s Spanish Civil War.
Their 2013 album "Savor Flamenco" won the Grammy Award for Best World Music Album in 2014.

The Gipsy Kings brought rumba flamenca to a global audience; their 1987 self-titled album, featuring "Bamboleo" and "Djobi Djoba," spent 40 weeks on the US charts, a rare feat for a Spanish-language record.

delaossa.fact: His acclaimed debut album, "Un Perro Andaluz" (2019), was made with producer J.Moods and featured 12 tracks.
Delaossa, whose real name is Daniel Martinez de la Ossa Romero (born 1993), is a Spanish rapper who grew up in El Palo, a traditionally fishing neighborhood of Malaga.
Around 2010 he was part of the Malaga rap crew Skill Leaders, which released the project "Skillbill" in 2012.
He first became interested in hip hop at just 12 years old.
In late 2015 he co-founded the artistic collective Space Hammu, also known as Space Hammurabi.
His 2020 mixtape "La Tour Liffee" featured collaborations with Israel B and Canary Islands rapper Cruz Cafune.
He has recorded with Argentine star Nicki Nicole, appearing on the 2021 song "Me Has Dejado."
He originally made music under the alias "Soup," releasing his first demo, "En blanco facil," in 2010.

antonio-jose.fact: His 'Te traigo flores' song was dedicated to his grandmother, who had recently passed away.
He has said it was his mother who signed him up for 'La Voz' by phone, not him.
His 2019 album 'Antídoto' was one of the best-selling records in Spain that year.
In 2022 he won the first edition of the TV show 'Dúos increíbles', teamed up with flamenco star Miguel Poveda.
Winning 'La Voz' earned him a deal with Universal Music, and his album 'El Viaje' was released just a month after his victory.
As a child he was also a keen footballer and finished second in a national futsal competition.
He was born on 2 January 1995 in Palma del Río, in the province of Córdoba.
At just 10 years old, Antonio José represented Spain at the 2005 Junior Eurovision Song Contest with 'Te traigo flores', finishing second by only three points.
He won the third season of Spain's 'La Voz' in 2015 as part of Antonio Orozco's team.

sergio-dalma.fact: He was born Josep Sergi Capdevila Querol in 1964 in Catalonia, and has recorded not only in Spanish but also in Catalan, Italian, English and French.
His 1989 debut single 'Esa chica es mía' became a hit across Spain and Latin America, and the album was certified platinum.
Between 2008 and 2013 he scored an unbroken run of five consecutive number one albums on the Spanish chart.
He is one of Spain's best-selling recording artists, having topped the official Spanish album chart nine times.
Sergio Dalma represented Spain at the Eurovision Song Contest 1991 in Rome with 'Bailar pegados', finishing in fourth place.
His popular 'Via Dalma' albums are collections of classic Italian songs reinterpreted in Spanish.
His career took off after he won the Catalan TV talent program 'Gent d'aquí', which led to a regular singing contract at a Barcelona nightclub.
'Bailar pegados' became his international breakthrough, reaching No. 6 on Billboard's U.S. Hot Latin Tracks chart and topping charts across Latin America.
In September 2014 he celebrated 25 years in music with a concert at Madrid's Las Ventas bullring, joined by guests including Pablo Alborán.
His 2010 album 'Via Dalma' was one of his biggest hits, spending 10 weeks at No. 1 in Spain and earning a six-times platinum certification.

alejandro-astola.fact: His music fuses traditional flamenco with rock, funk and jazz, a style often described as 'flamenco-underground'.
In 2017 he teamed up with Diego Pozo 'El Ratón' to release the live album 'Gargantas callejeras y guitarras de cartón'.
The band's 2007 debut album 'Contracorriente' spawned the video 'Escúchame mujer', which quickly surpassed 20 million views on YouTube.
He was born in Seville on 9 April 1990 and first picked up a guitar at age 12, teaching himself to play in just four months before starting to write his own songs.
Fondo Flamenco's 2005 demo 'Ojalá' became an internet hit, sparking a tour of more than 80 concerts across Andalusia.
He personally hand-delivered the crowdfunded albums door to door to the fans who had backed the project.
Alejandro Astola was the founder and main songwriter of the hugely popular Andalusian band Fondo Flamenco before launching his solo career.
He made his solo debut in 2015 with the double album 'Rockallano', financed through a crowdfunding campaign that raised 14,500 euros.
Alongside his music he founded Rockallano S.L., his own record label, publishing house, management and video production company.

black-coffee.fact: His 2021 album 'Subconsciously' won the Grammy Award for Best Dance/Electronic Album at the 64th Annual Grammy Awards.
He majored in Jazz Studies at Technikon Natal, now the Durban University of Technology, and started out as a backing singer.
He founded his own record label, Soulistic Music, in 2005 and released his self-titled debut album that same year.
He contributed to the beat of 'Get It Together' on Drake's 2017 album 'More Life', and later co-wrote and co-produced three songs on Drake's 2022 album 'Honestly, Nevermind'.

In 1990, while celebrating Nelson Mandela's release from prison, a teenage Black Coffee was struck by a car and permanently lost the use of his left arm, yet he went on to become one of the world's most acclaimed DJs.
His real name is Nkosinathi Innocent Maphumulo, and he was born on 11 March 1976 in eThekwini (Durban), South Africa.
His accolades include eight South African Music Awards, four DJ Awards and two Metro FM Awards, in addition to his Grammy.
He collaborated with David Guetta on the 2018 single 'Drive' featuring Delilah Montagu, and teamed up with Usher on the 2019 track 'LaLaLa'.
In 2010 he DJed for 60 hours non-stop at Maponya Mall in Soweto in a bid for a Guinness World Record.
He became the first South African artist to sell out a headline show at New York's Madison Square Garden.

vanesa-martin.fact: Her albums have gone gold and platinum in Spain — 'Munay' (2016) topped the charts and earned platinum certification.
She has sat in the coach's chair on Spain's television talent show 'La Voz Kids'.
In 2019 she was among the winners of the Premios Cadena Dial, which honour Spain's top artists of the year.
Before music took over, she earned degrees in Teaching and Pedagogy at the University of Málaga.
At the 2020 Premios Odeón she was named Best Female Artist.
Her father gave her her first guitar at age six, and by fifteen she was performing in Málaga venues and on local radio.
Her 2018 album 'Todas las mujeres que habitan en mí' was recorded in Los Angeles and went platinum, selling more than 40,000 copies.
In 2024 she signed with Universal Music Spain after more than a decade on Warner Music.
Beyond music, she's a published poet — her 2016 book 'Mujer Océano' collected her verse.
Vanesa Martín is a malagueña — born in Málaga in 1980 — so her Costa del Sol dates are a genuine hometown homecoming.

lola-indigo.fact: Born Miriam Doblas Munoz in Madrid, she was raised in Huetor-Tajar, a small town in the province of Granada, Andalusia.
She won the MTV Europe Music Award for Best Spanish Act in both 2019 and 2024.
Since 2024 she has served as a coach on Spain's "La Voz Kids."
Her 2018 debut single "Ya No Quiero Na" was certified triple platinum in Spain, and its low-budget music video passed a million views in a single day.
Before her singing career, she worked as a professional backup dancer for stars including Chris Brown, Enrique Iglesias and Miguel Bose, and lived in China for three years.
Although she was eliminated early from the 2017 series of "Operacion Triunfo," she went on to become one of Spain's biggest pop stars.
Her debut studio album "Akelarre" (2019) - Basque for "witches' sabbath" - debuted at number one on the Spanish charts.
In 2018 she competed on the celebrity impersonation show "Tu Cara Me Suena," finishing fourth.
Her "High (Remix)" with Maria Becerra and Tini was named Billboard's Best Latin Summer Remix of 2020.

malu.fact: She has recorded with fellow Spanish stars including Alejandro Sanz and Melendi.
Her 2013 album Sí entered the Spanish albums chart at number one and stayed on the chart for more than a year.
She has released around a dozen studio albums and sold millions of records across Spain and Latin America.
Her real name is María Lucía Sánchez Benítez — 'Malú' is a childhood nickname.
Malú was a coach on La Voz (The Voice Spain) across several seasons, mentoring the country's rising singers.
Her 2010 album Guerra Fría, featuring the hit 'Blanco y Negro,' was one of her biggest commercial successes.
She was discovered at 15 singing at a family party; her 1998 debut album Aprendiz went multi-platinum in Spain.
Flamenco runs in the family: Malú is the daughter of singer Pepe de Lucía and the niece of the legendary guitarist Paco de Lucía.

nina-pastori.fact: She recorded her debut album 'Entre dos puertos' at just 17, produced by Paco Ortega and Alejandro Sanz; it went platinum.
Legendary flamenco singer Camarón de la Isla, also from her hometown of San Fernando, Cádiz, was among her first mentors.
Her stage name comes from being known as 'la niña de la Pastori' — her mother was the flamenco singer 'La Pastori'.
Niña Pastori has won four Latin Grammy Awards — three for Best Flamenco Album and one for Best Folk Album.
She is the only flamenco artist to have been nominated for the Grammy Award for Best Latin Pop Album.
In 2018 she was awarded the Medalla de Andalucía, and she performed the Andalusian anthem at the ceremony.
Her early hit 'Cai', written by Alejandro Sanz, is a tribute to the city of Cádiz.
She sang a version of Schubert's 'Ave Maria' during Pope John Paul II's last visit to Madrid in May 2003, before some three million people.
As a child she performed in flamenco tablaos with her mother from age six, and at seven won a singing contest at the El Chato club in San Fernando.
On the 2014 album 'Raíz', made with Lila Downs and Soledad Pastorutti, she collaborated with Santana on the track 'Una Noche en Nápoles'.

the-blue-stompers-jump-review.fact: Their sound blends boogie woogie, Afro-American blues, 1940s New Orleans jazz and the raw R&B of Dr. Feelgood.
Their guitarist Inaki Moreno has more than 25 years dedicated to the blues, drawing on the raw, effects-free styles of John Lee Hooker, Buddy Guy and Muddy Waters.
Stylianou cites blues harmonica greats Little Walter, James Harman, James Cotton and Kim Wilson among his biggest influences.
The blues group is based in Fuengirola, on Spain's Malaga coast.
The Blue Stompers Jump Review are a multinational Costa del Sol blues band, described as a hidden gem with members from the UK, Cyprus, Finland and Spain.
The band was formed in 2014 by front man and harmonica player Paul Stylianou.
They have toured the blues circuit across Spain and Europe, playing venues from Ain't Nothin' But the Blues Bar in London to the Kwadendamme Blues Festival in the Netherlands.
Frontman Paul Stylianou is originally from Greenwich in London and moved to Spain in 2002, playing with blues bands along the Costa del Sol before forming the group.
